issues.description: The controller method for creating a person (POST /persons) has a different return type in the template and the solution. In the template PersonResource.createPerson returns ResponseEntity<Person> and returns the saved entity (lines 37-43). In the solution PersonResource.createPerson is declared void and does not return the saved Person (lines 37-43). This mismatch can confuse students when they compare their controller implementation to the reference solution and when they expect a saved Person object in the HTTP response body (e.g., in integration tests or when chaining requests).
issues.suggested_fix: Align the controller method signatures between template and solution. Choose one consistent return type and use it in both repositories. Recommended: have createPerson return ResponseEntity<Person> (the saved entity) in both template and solution so clients/tests can consume the created resource. Alternatively, document the void behavior clearly and update the template and tests accordingly.
